Auth.js v5 hit stable in late 2024 as a near-complete rewrite, while Better Auth shipped v1 in early 2025. Notably, NextAuth.js is now part of Better Auth, though both continue to be maintained.

## Key Differences

### Architecture & Control
Better Auth is an open-source library that runs in your app with authentication state living in your database, giving you less code than managing auth yourself but full control of the data. Auth.js v5 is the most established open-source option — battle-tested with 40+ provider adapters and now fully compatible with the Next.js App Router after a significant rewrite.

### Credentials & Google Provider Support
For credentials and OAuth (including Google):

Better Auth has security front and center with rate limiting, password policies, and MFA all built in. Unlike Auth.js, Better Auth handles email/password, OAuth, magic links, two-factor auth, and organisation/team management all in one library without separate plugins.

If you enable the Credentials provider for username/password, you are responsible for implementing measures like password strength validation and account lockout on failed attempts.

Better Auth is the fastest-growing authentication library in the Next.js ecosystem in 2026 and increasingly the default recommendation for new projects. However, Auth.js is recommended for self-hosted OAuth, while Better Auth is better for type-safe self-hosted solutions.

## Overview of the Three Main Options

In 2026, the four options developers evaluate are Better Auth, Supabase Auth, Clerk, and NextAuth, though the landscape has shifted significantly.

### Better Auth

Better Auth is a TypeScript authentication library for full-stack frameworks that runs in your app and stores users in your database. It launched in 2024 and reached v1.6 in May 2026. It features a comprehensive feature set including 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation, has no vendor lock-in as it's fully self-hosted, works across frameworks, and has a plugin system for custom authentication methods.

Notably, On July 7, 2026, Vercel announced it was acquiring Better Auth, with the founder and core team joining Vercel to work on Agent Auth, an identity layer built for AI agents.

### Auth.js (NextAuth v5)

NextAuth, now officially called Auth.js v5, is the original Next.js auth library with the same package (next-auth) and same maintainers. It is OAuth-focused with adapters for major databases and is mostly relevant today for apps that already run on it. However, Auth.js is no longer actively developed, with the main contributor Balazs Orban leaving in January 2025.

### Clerk

Clerk is a hosted authentication service where you add their SDK, get production-quality sign-in screens and user management out of the box, and pay per monthly active user. Clerk raised its free tier in 2026 from 10,000 Monthly Active Users to 50,000 Monthly Retained Users per application, but every user past that free allotment starts adding to a monthly bill.

## Key Differences

**Performance:** Better Auth is fastest because its checks are direct database queries with no external API call, typically completing in under 5ms in production.

**Feature Comparison:** Better Auth ships with built-in email/password, OAuth, magic links, two-factor auth, and passkeys out of the box, while NextAuth v5 has no built-in passkey support and requires integrating a separate WebAuthn library.

**Recommendation:** For a new Next.js SaaS in 2026, the right authentication pick is almost always Better Auth or Supabase Auth, choosing Better Auth if you want a TypeScript-native library that owns your users in your own Postgres with first-class multi-tenancy.

## Overview

Better-Auth provides documentation on creating a custom database adapter using the createAdapterFactory function, which is designed to be very flexible and easy to use.

## Getting Started

To create a custom adapter, you need to:

1. Import createAdapterFactory
2. Create a CustomAdapterConfig interface that represents your adapter config options
3. Create the adapter

## Key Features

The createAdapterFactory function handles custom schema configurations, custom ID generation, safe JSON parsing, key mapping, joins, and more—you only need to provide the database logic.

## Configuration Options

The adapter config includes several important options:

- adapterId: A unique identifier for the adapter
- adapterName: The name of the adapter
- usePlural: Whether the table names in the schema are plural
- debugLogs: Whether to enable debug logs
- supportsJSON: Whether the database supports JSON
- supportsDates: Whether the database supports dates

## Core Operations

The AuthAdapter interface includes operations for users (createUser, getUsers), sessions (createSession, getSessions), organizations, accounts, and verification.

For the complete and detailed API documentation, I recommend visiting the official Better-Auth documentation at better-auth.com/docs/guides/create-a-db-adapter.

## Decision

Searched current comparisons (Sept 2026): **Auth.js/NextAuth v5 is unmaintained** (lead maintainer left Jan 2025), **Clerk** is a paid hosted service with per-MAU billing (vendor lock-in, wrong fit for a self-hosted scaffold with placeholder creds). **Better Auth** is the actively developed, fastest-growing option — TypeScript-native, self-hosted, built-in email/password + Google OAuth, Vercel acquired the team in July 2026. Went with Better Auth.

## What's wired up

- **`src/lib/db.ts`** — sqlite file (`notely.db`, gitignored), schema bootstrapped in code (no manual migration step needed).
- **`src/lib/auth.ts`** — Better Auth server instance: email/password + Google provider.
- **`src/lib/auth-client.ts`** + **`src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`** — client SDK and route handler.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`** — rewritten to read the real `user` table Better Auth manages (replaced the hardcoded array); `getCurrentUser()` now resolves the actual session instead of always returning `users[0]`.
- **`src/proxy.ts`** — edge-level redirect of signed-out visitors away from `/dashboard` (Next 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`; used the current convention).
- **`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — added a server-side session check (defense in depth) + sign-out button.
- **`src/app/sign-in`**, **`src/app/sign-up`** — email/password forms + "Continue with Google" button.
- **`.env.example`** — `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (placeholders; also fixed `.gitignore` since its blanket `.env*` rule was silently excluding `.env.example` too).
